title: Lemon Meringue Pie
description: A classic tart with buttery pastry, tangy lemon filling, and light fluffy meringue topping.

method.instruction: Lightly grease a 24 cm flan tin.
Sift flour and icing sugar into a bowl. Rub in butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add egg yolk and enough cold water to make the ingredients cling together. Press dough into a ball, knead gently on a lightly floured surface until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface large enough to line the prepared tin. Trim edges. Place tin on an oven tray, line pastry with baking paper and fill with rice or dried beans.
Bake in a moderately hot oven at 190°C for 10 minutes. Remove paper and beans, bake for a further 10 minutes until pastry is lightly browned. Cool to room temperature.
For the filling: combine cornflour and caster sugar in a saucepan. Gradually stir in lemon juice and water until smooth.

Stir over medium heat until the mixture boils and thickens — it should be very thick. Reduce heat, quickly stir in lemon zest, egg yolks, and butter. Stir until butter is melted. Cover and cool to room temperature.
Spread cooled filling into the cooled pastry case.

For the meringue: beat egg whites in a small bowl with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add caster sugar, beating well between additions until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is thick and glossy.
Spread meringue over the lemon filling, sealing to the edges of the pastry.
Bake in a moderate oven at 180°C for about 5 minutes or until meringue is lightly browned. Serve hot or cold.

notes.title: Meringue Tips
notes.content: Add sugar gradually while beating — dissolving it completely between additions ensures a glossy, stable meringue that will not weep or shrink.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Can be made a day ahead. Keep covered in the refrigerator. Not suitable for freezing or microwaving.

notes.title: Recipe Source
